entries.name: AgentCron Register Schedule
entries.description: Register a persistent cron schedule that fires HTTP requests to a target URL on a fixed interval. Survives agent session termination; runs server-side even when the agent is offline. Pay-per-registration in USDC on Base mainnet.

usage.callShape: POST https://cron.memoryapi.org/x402/cron/register with JSON body {agent_id, url, interval_minutes, method?, headers?, body?, duration_days?}
usage.outputShape: unverified (paid call blocked as provisioning op); OpenAPI implies a schedule object likely with schedule_id + status fields, retrievable via GET /x402/cron/status?schedule_id=
quirks: REAL schema from OpenAPI (https://cron.memoryapi.org/openapi.json), NOT empirical 400-probing as the old registry usage claimed. Required: agent_id, url, interval_minutes. Optional: method (default GET), headers (object), body (string), duration_days (integer, max 30, default 7).
interval_minutes is an INTEGER with minimum 15 (>=15) — NOT a cron expression string. interval_minutes:60 = hourly. Values <15 will be rejected.
duration_days caps at 30; the schedule auto-expires after this many days.

PROVISIONING/RECURRING op: registering creates a persistent server-side job that repeatedly calls the target URL. Auto-mode classifier blocks the paid call as an outward/provisioning action. Point url only at an endpoint you control.
CHARGE-ON-VALIDATION-FAILURE (per prior QA): each malformed POST still costs $0.05 — build the full valid body before calling.
Management endpoints exist in OpenAPI: POST /x402/cron/cancel (reversible), GET /x402/cron/status, GET /x402/cron/history — but all GET reads currently return broken empty-402 (see alerts service).
usage.guide: Register a persistent cron schedule that fires HTTP requests to a target URL on a fixed interval. Survives agent session termination; runs server-side even when the agent is offline. Pay-per-registration in USDC on Base mainnet. entries.name: AgentCron Alerts
entries.description: Intended GET read endpoint at /x402/cron/alerts ($0.001). Not present in the provider OpenAPI spec and currently non-functional.

usage.outputShape: none — endpoint returns 402 with empty {} body; never reached a 2xx
quirks: BROKEN: /x402/cron/alerts is NOT in the provider OpenAPI spec (only /register, /status, /cancel, /history are documented).
Returns HTTP 402 with an EMPTY {} body and NO x402 'accepts' challenge — payment cannot be completed. Verified via raw curl AND via MCP agentcash fetch (both got 402 + empty body, paid:false).
Same empty-402 pattern affects the documented GET reads /status and /history too — appears to be an upstream x402 challenge bug on all GET endpoints.
REGISTRY FIX: replace /alerts with the spec'd /x402/cron/status?schedule_id=...&agent_id=... once the empty-402 challenge is fixed upstream.
usage.guide: Intended GET read endpoint at /x402/cron/alerts ($0.001). Not present in the provider OpenAPI spec and currently non-functional. GET https://cron.memoryapi.org/x402/cron/alerts?agent_id=<id> (no body) Output: none — endpoint returns 402 with empty {} body; never reached a 2xx

entries.name: Cron-as-a-Service
entries.description: Schedule webhook calls on a cron expression (MCP webhook scheduler). Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://cron-service.replit.app/api/mcp/sse (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453, 0.001 USDC) — but this is an MCP/SSE endpoint, not a working one-shot paid HTTP call
usage.outputShape: Intended (per advertised example, NOT achieved): body.job_id, body.status, body.scheduled_at, body.message. In practice the paid GET only returns the unpaid 402 discovery body (body.error = 'X-Payment header is required').
quirks: Paid x402 GET did NOT settle: payProvider ran the flow but the server returned the SAME unpaid 402 challenge ('X-Payment header is required') with paid:false, costUsd:0, no txHash. No money moved.
URL path is /api/mcp/sse — this is an MCP Server-Sent-Events surface, not a plain paid REST endpoint. A one-shot HTTP GET only fetches the x402 discovery 402; it does not execute a schedule.

No input surface to actually schedule a job: registry inputSchema is empty {} and the 402's accepts.outputSchema.input is {type:'http', method:'GET', queryParams:{}} with NO field for a target webhook URL or cron expression. You cannot tell it WHAT to schedule or WHEN over this call shape.

To use this service for real you would need to speak the MCP protocol (initialize + tools/call over SSE/JSON-RPC) with x402 payment on the tool call, not a single GET — out of scope for the registry's call-shape model.
usage.guide: Do not call this as a simple paid HTTP GET — it does not work that way. The endpoint at https://cron-service.replit.app/api/mcp/sse is an MCP Server-Sent-Events surface; a one-shot GET only returns the x402 discovery 402 ('X-Payment header is required') even after the payment flow runs, and never settles a charge. There is also no input field (empty schema; queryParams only) to specify the webhook URL or cron expression you'd want to schedule, so the documented {job_id,status,scheduled_at} response is unreachable via this call shape. Treat as broken for registry use; revisit only via a full MCP client (initialize + tools/call with x402 on the tool call).

entries.name: Spraay Cron Create
entries.description: Create a recurring scheduled job (cron) on the Spraay gateway. The job fires a chosen action on a standard 5-field cron schedule with an action-specific payload. Supported actions include webhook.trigger, batch.execute, payroll.execute, swap.execute, bridge.execute, notify.email, notify.sms, xmtp.send, analytics.snapshot, invoice.remind. Provisions a persistent resource that fires on schedule.

usage.callShape: POST https://gateway.spraay.app/api/v1/cron/create with JSON body {action, schedule, payload, maxRuns?}
usage.outputShape: id (string, e.g. cron_1780972938100_j9j49t), status (string, e.g. 'active'); confirmed via cron/list job entries: jobs[].{id,action,schedule,status,nextRun,lastRun,runCount}
quirks: registry inputSchema was null; REAL required body fields are action, schedule, payload (a naive {name,url,method} returns 400 'Missing required fields: action, schedule, payload')

action must be one of a fixed enum, NOT a free string: batch.execute, payroll.execute, swap.execute, bridge.execute, webhook.trigger, notify.email, notify.sms, xmtp.send, analytics.snapshot, invoice.remind
schedule is a standard 5-field cron expression (e.g. '0 0 * * *')
payload is an object whose shape depends on the action (webhook.trigger: {url, method}; batch.execute: {token, recipients}; etc.)
maxRuns (number) is an OPTIONAL field to cap total executions
endpoint charges $0.01 per POST even on a 400 validation error — get the body shape right BEFORE paying
PROVISIONS a persistent scheduled job (outward/irreversible side effects on schedule) — NOT auto-verified; auto-mode classifier blocks the paid create call
x402 paid on Base USDC (amount 10000 = $0.01); also accepts Solana USDC; create response is sync (no async polling)
created jobs are scoped to the calling wallet and appear in cron/list
usage.guide: Create a recurring scheduled job (cron) on the Spraay gateway. The job fires a chosen action on a standard 5-field cron schedule with an action-specific payload. Supported actions include webhook.trigger, batch.execute, payroll.execute, swap.execute, bridge.execute, notify.email, notify.sms, xmtp.send, analytics.snapshot, invoice.remind. Provisions a persistent resource that fires on schedule. POST https://gateway.spraay.app/api/v1/cron/create with JSON body {action, schedule, payload, maxRuns?} Output: id (string, e.g. cron_1780972938100_j9j49t), status (string, e.g. 'active'); confirmed via cron/list job entries: jobs[].{id,action,schedule,status,nextRun,lastRun,runCount}

entries.name: Cron Expression Explainer
entries.description: Parse any 5/6/7-field cron expression (or @yearly/@monthly/@weekly/@daily/@hourly macro) into a human-readable explanation: validates syntax, breaks out each field, detects the common pattern name, computes the next N run times, and assigns a quality score/grade. Lets agents understand and validate cron schedules without implementing their own parser.

usage.callShape: DEFAULT (netintel): GET with query-string params only, NO body — expression (required, URL-encode spaces as %20 and asterisks as %2A), timezone (IANA, default UTC), count (default 5, max 20). ALTERNATE gateways (deployer cron-explain, deployer cron-parse, agentutility cron-explain) take a POST JSON body {expression (required), timezone}; these share one x402-deployer app and are the same operation under different slugs.
usage.outputShape: netintel GET: { expression, is_valid (bool), fields:{minute,hour,day_of_month,month,day_of_week}, explanation (string), pattern_name (string), next_runs (ISO8601 string[]), warnings (string[]), score (number 0-100), grade (string A-F), findings (array) }. deployer/agentutility POST (leaner, unpaid/from spec): { explanation (string), frequency (string bucket e.g. 'daily'), plus validation flag and runs-per-day estimate }.
quirks: Default backend (netintel) is a GET endpoint: pass expression/timezone/count as URL query-string params, NOT a JSON body, despite registry inputSchema being object-shaped.
expression must be URL-encoded on the GET backend (space -> %20, asterisk -> %2A).
GET x402 flow on netintel could not be completed by qa-pay (empty 402 body); verified instead via MCP agentcash fetch which paid $0.001 and returned the body.

x402.agentutility.ai and x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev are the SAME deployed app ('x402-deployer' v1, payTo 0x6c0752c09e7F6fA6526fCDf40e456a159ebB5621, network eip155:8453); not independent providers.
On the x402-deployer app, /cron-parse and /cron-explain are explicitly the same backend under two slugs (per its own endpoint catalog).
POST backends hang on a payment-less request (no immediate 402 body); their schema was read from the deployer root catalog (GET / returns full endpoint list with input_schema/input_example).
Supports 5-, 6-, and 7-field cron plus @macro shorthands.
Output field names differ by gateway: netintel returns fields/next_runs/score/grade; deployer returns frequency. Normalize on 'explanation' which both provide.

entries.name: Natural Language to Cron
entries.description: Convert a natural-language schedule (e.g. 'every weekday at 9:30am') into a standard 5-field cron expression. Returns the cron string, a human-readable summary, and the next 5 fire times computed in the requested IANA timezone.

usage.callShape: POST JSON body { text (required, natural-language schedule, maxLength 500), timezone (IANA string, default UTC) }.
usage.outputShape: { cron (string, 5-field cron expression), human_readable (string), timezone (string), next_fires (ISO8601 string[], next 5 fire times in the given timezone, rendered as UTC instants) }
quirks: This is the INVERSE of the explainer (text -> cron, not cron -> text); it was entirely missing from the original bundled usage doc.
POST JSON body with key 'text' (NOT 'expression') — different field name from the explainer op; passing 'expression' will fail.
next_fires are ISO8601 instants in UTC (e.g. 13:30:00.000Z for a 9:30am America/New_York schedule), even though scheduling is computed in the requested timezone.
Always returns a 5-field cron expression.
Provider origin x402.nichospt.net publishes a full OpenAPI spec at /openapi.json; x402 network is Solana per its spec, but qa-pay settled the call on Base ($0.01).
usage.guide: Convert a natural-language schedule (e.g. 'every weekday at 9:30am') into a standard 5-field cron expression. POST JSON body { text (required, natural-language schedule, maxLength 500), timezone (IANA string, default UTC) }.
